card.title: Exam bank — every board question on elasticity

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three questions, one method: define stress/strain/Y with units (2023), repeat Y alone (2023), then compute stress and strain for the steel wire (2022: 100 N on 2 mm squared gives 5x10^7 Pa stress, 2.5x10^-4 strain). Stress is force per area, strain is fractional change (unitless), Y is their ratio — stiffness priced in pascals.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: stress = F/A (Pa) · strain = dL/L (unitless) · Y = stress/strain = FL/A dL · U = half stress strain volume

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Hooke and Y hold within the ELASTIC limit only — past yield the ratio collapses (meaning stiffness is a small-strain property). Strain's unitlessness is why Y inherits stress units. Steel's Y ~2x10^11 Pa is the benchmark that makes wire extensions millimetric.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Strain has NO unit — writing 'strain in Pa' fails instantly. Bulk/shear moduli extend the idea to volume/shape; Poisson couples stretch to thinning. The 2022 wire: strain 2.5x10^-4 means a 1 m wire stretches 0.25 mm.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2022 (3): stress = 100/(2x10^-6) = 5x10^7 Pa; strain = stress/Y = 5x10^7/2x10^11 = 2.5x10^-4. NEB 2023 (3+2): stress (Pa), strain (none), Y = stress/strain (Pa) — definitions first, substitution second, unit check last.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: units on strain; mm squared left unconverted (2 mm2 = 2x10^-6 m2); applying Hooke past yield. Moduli are small-strain averages — temperature, defects and rate shift real values.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Energy density: dW = F dx with F = (YA/L)x integrates to half stress times strain times volume — the triangular area under the Hookean line. No other derivation is asked; definitions plus this energy form cover the unit.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Define + units' opens most elasticity questions — write all three with units in one block. Numericals: convert mm2 to m2 first, then stress, then strain. Y in Pa always; strain never has units.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): stress, strain, Y + SI units. NEB 2023 (2): Y definition + formula + unit. NEB 2022 (3): 100 N on 2 mm2 wire — stress, then strain.
